blocks.content: Avoidable negative marks from misreading questions often make the difference between selection and rejection.

rows: Uses precise, measured, or conditional terms
Matches a common miscalculation or partial step
Derived from complete and verified execution
May require careful verification against prompt

items: Always re-read the final clause of the question stem to confirm if it asks for 'True' or 'Not True'.
Watch out for distractor options in quantitative aptitude that represent intermediate calculation steps.
Never attempt random guessing without eliminating at least two options under negative marking schemes.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Misreading qualifier words like 'NOT' or 'INCORRECT' in questions leads to heavy negative penalty.
Options containing absolute terms like 'Always', 'Never', or 'Only' are frequently designed as traps.
Spending over 2 minutes on a single complex question disrupts overall exam strategy.
Inserting external unstated assumptions into critical reasoning questions causes avoidable errors.
